text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"Time restricted eating reduced total daily energy intake for many participants and produced weight loss over twelve week trials.","cited_pids":["fasting#0"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"Some participants found an eating window easier to follow than continuous restriction.","cited_pids":["fasting#1","fasting#3"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"Reduced evening snacking helped account for part of the calorie deficit in time restricted eating.","cited_pids":["fasting#1","fasting#3"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"Head to head trials matching total calories found no weight loss advantage of intermittent fasting over continuous restriction across twelve months.","cited_pids":["fasting#4"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"Benefits of fasting in short trials largely disappeared once total energy intake was controlled.","cited_pids":["fasting#7"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"Dropout rates in fasting arms exceeded those in standard restriction arms in several studies.","cited_pids":["fasting#6"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"Intermittent fasting supports weight loss only insofar as it creates an energy deficit.","cited_pids":[]}]}
